context: Sachiko-grandma teaches Hina-young how to make a paper crane.
purpose: Grandmother teaching child traditional craft; quiet attention.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.en: First, fold it in half for me.
lines.style: Warm, patient opening. Soft hands in her voice. Each instruction clear and unhurried, like she's done this a hundred times and has all the time in the world for this one.

lines.speaker: hina_child
lines.style: Bright and eager, checking in. Small upward lift at the end—genuine question, not performance. The concentrated attention of a child who wants to get it right.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、上手ね、ゆっくりで。
lines.en: Perfect, you're doing beautifully. Take your time.
lines.style: Soft praise settling over the words. No rush. Gentle encouragement on 'beautifully'—grandmother noticing not just the action but the care in it.

lines.speaker: hina_child
lines.en: I can see the shape appearing!
lines.style: Delighted recognition breaking through. Quick, bright—the genuine excitement of watching something familiar emerge. A child's wonder at the magic of folded paper.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.style: Reverent, nearly whispered weight to it. Settling into something larger than this moment—generations of hands, this shape. Tender and ceremonial without being stiff.
